paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. This whole psalm is one long "thank you" that starts with a reason. The writer doesn't just feel thankful. He looks at what the LORD has done and says, "Great are the works of the LORD; they are pondered by all who delight in them." (Psalm 111:2) So a thankful heart isn't something you squeeze out of yourself. It grows when you slow down and really look at what God has done.

Now look at what the psalmist finds when he looks. God provides, God remembers His covenant, and God has "sent redemption to His people." (Psalm 111:5, 9) His precepts are "trustworthy," and they are "upheld forever and ever." (Psalm 111:7, 8) I've been in a place where everything around me was fading, so hear me: a God who doesn't fade is GOOD news. You can build a whole life on what He says.

That's why the psalm ends where it does: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all who follow His precepts gain rich understanding." (Psalm 111:10) Wisdom starts with knowing who God is, holy and awesome, and then it grows as you follow what He says. So when you open the Word, baker, bring a heart ready to ponder and ready to follow. Start there, and your praise will keep going, because "His praise endures forever!" (Psalm 111:10)
